subject: Renewal: VPC tenant forks + capacity bridging request
messages:
From: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@medsyn.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: salesops@medsyn.com
Date: 2027-05-12T09:42:00-04:00
Subject: Renewal request + new VPC tenant forks and isolation requirements

Hi Naomi,

We're coming up on our Redwood renewal in July and procurement has asked for a simple plan: we need to add two isolated VPC tenant forks to support a new analytics environment for our partner integrations. High-level asks:

- Two additional isolated tenants (us-east) with strict network isolation (no cross-tenant peering)
- Dedicated cluster per tenant with capacity for ~120 qps peak inference across short bursts
- A 12-month term extension starting from renewal date; we'd like pricing for both 12- and 24-month options
- SOC2 evidence & SSO integration notes for procurement

I attached a short requirements PDF (MediSyn-Renewal-Req.pdf). Can you share an SOW and an estimate for the uplift? Also flag any lead times for provisioning on-prem or dedicated nodes.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Integrations
MediSyn Health

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@medsyn.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-13T11:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request + new VPC tenant forks and isolation requirements

Alex —

Thanks for the clear outline. Happy to coordinate the renewal and the tenant forks. Quick notes and asks to scope the SOW accurately:

- Can you confirm expected steady-state qps vs peak burst (you mentioned ~120 qps peak; is steady-state ~20-30 qps?)
- Any dataset residency constraints beyond US-east (e.g., do logs need to be sequestered to a separate S3 bucket with restricted access?)
- Will the new tenants require their own KMS keys or can they use a shared customer-managed key?

Attached is an initial capacity worksheet (initial-capacity-worksheet.xlsx) — if you can fill the second tab with typical request distribution and samples/day we can firm up node sizing.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical working session this week (30–45 min) with Priyom to lock sizing and lead times
- Commercial note from Ben with 12/24 month pricing scenarios and isolation premium
- Draft SOW for review (we'll include provisioning windows and rollback/fallback clauses)

I'm cc'ing Ben and Priyom; what times work for you on Thursday or Friday?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@medsyn.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-13T15:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request + new VPC tenant forks and isolation requirements

Alex / Naomi —

Quick technical read from infra: assuming the 120 qps peak is across aggregate inference endpoints, our initial recommendation is:

- Provision 2 dedicated clusters (one per tenant) each with 4x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes to start. This gives headroom for model warm caches and burst handling.
- If you enable prefix/KV cache reuse across endpoints within each tenant, we can reduce to 3x nodes per cluster after a 2-week warm-up and traffic observation window.
- Expected provisioning lead time (hosted Dedicated): 2–3 weeks for capacity reservation in us-east; on-prem or private airgapped adds 4–6 weeks depending on shipment and network approvals.
- Data segregation: recommend separate S3 buckets + per-tenant KMS keys. If procurement insists on HSM-backed keys we'll add configuration & audit tasks to the SOW.

Attaching a capacity matrix (capacity-matrix.xlsx) with node-level t-shirt-sizing and token-cost estimates.

I'll join the technical call and can run a quick traffic profile exercise during the session.

— Priyom (Infra Solutions Engineer)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@medsyn.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-14T09:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request + new VPC tenant forks and isolation requirements

Alex —

Appreciate the context. Commercial summary below (high-level; final numbers will go in the SOW):

Option A — 12-month term (start at renewal):
- Base renewal (existing footprint): $320k/year
- Two isolated tenant forks (dedicated clusters): +$95k/year per tenant (isolation premium + fixed node allocation)
- One-time provisioning and SOW fees: $12k
- Expected discount for multi-year committment: 0% (12-month)

Option B — 24-month term:
- Base renewal locked at $300k/year (price protected)
- Tenant forks: $85k/year per tenant
- One-time provisioning and SOW fees: $10k
- Suggested upsell credit if you commit to model quantization advisory (we can include Optimize credits)

Notes:
- We can consider an SLA exception for the isolated tenants with a small additional fee; I'll flag that in the SOW.
- Link to the draft deal record: https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/DEAL-4539

I'll prepare a strawman SOW and attach for quick review. If you're aligned with the 24-month option, there's room to tighten pricing and absorb some provisioning fees.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(Attachment: SOW-draft.pdf)

From: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@medsyn.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Ben / Naomi —

Thanks — the 24-month option with price protection looks favorable. A few procurement asks before we sign:

- Please share the formal SOW and a DocuSign link for signature
- We need SOC2 artifacts (latest report) and a short note on key management (KMS vs HSM) to attach to our purchase order
- Can you confirm the provisioning lead time again for dedicated clusters in us-east? Procurement will plan cost recognition based on delivery dates.

If you can get the SOW & DocuSign by EOD Wednesday we should be able to fast-track the PO.

Alex
